audit.action: cite a better source for the same coding
audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed final stress, dominant/rightmost: stress moves to the last suffix vowel) rests on the standard reference grammar of the language, Roos 2000 (Leiden PhD, 431 pp.), sec. 2.10 p.35. We previously held no copy; the cited Wayback scan was fetched sources now and the quotation confirmed verbatim on the page image and by scanned. No better stress source exists in the accessible literature: Glottolog's larger items are a Chinese-language grammar (Chen 2004, print only) and Zhong's 2019 ANU thesis (request-only), and the one experimental paper found (Lyu 2019, fetched sources) agrees with final, suffix-shifting stress. Nothing suggests a recode. The record's grade field is empty and 'held' was empty; with the primary source now on file and verified, the evidence grade can be set to primary-source-verified. Optional refinement from the same passage: domain = word including suffixes, with enc

sources.citation: Roos 2000, The Western Yugur (Yellow Uygur) Language, sec. 2.10 Word stress, p.35 - full page re-read as image from Wayback PDF of members.home.nl/marcmarti/yugur (431-pp. scan)
sources.quote: Stress is on the final vowel of the word; if a suffix containing a vowel is added to a word, the stress shifts to this vowel. The evidential particle -ti (see 7.3.2.) is usually unstressed, but the pronunciation changes to -tv when it bears emphatic stress.

sources.quote: Stress is on the final vowel of the word; if a suffix containing a vowel is added to a word, the stress shifts to this vowel. The evidential particle -tï is usually unstressed (emphatic -tʋ); likewise question particle mi (stressed mʋ).

sources.citation: Lyu, Shiliang. 2019. Acoustic Energy Analysis of Vowels in Western Yugur Language. Proceedings ADLH 2019 (webofproceedings.org, ADLH19011), pp. 56-59 approx.
sources.quote: 'In the western Yugur language, the accent of a polysyllabic word is usually on the last syllable ... If the word has an additional component, such as an increase in the syllable within the word, the position of the accent will shift back' ; 'the accented syllables are located at the end of the word'; stress is non-distinctive.

sources.note: Only instrumental (intensity) look at Western Yugur word stress found; weak venue but independently reports final stress shifting rightward with suffixation.
